key_insight: A link-aware initialization plus plain gradient descent can recover latent factor models with missing, non-Gaussian data and still provide valid uncertainty quantification, thanks to implicit regularization and rowwise error control.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical, nonconvex inference pipeline for large sparse systems—useful when you need scalable estimation and confidence bands without extra debiasing steps.
method: Double-SVD initialization adapted to the exponential-family link
Unilateral refinement to achieve rowwise consistency and enter a contraction region
Vanilla gradient descent with implicit regularization to reach statistical error
evidence_signal: The abstract reports asymptotically valid individual and simultaneous inference, minimax-rate estimation up to logarithmic factors, and supporting simulations plus an LLM evaluation application.
watch_item: Performance depends on the initializer entering the incoherence/contraction regime, so severe model misspecification or poor link specification could weaken guarantees.
paper_title: From Good Starts to Optimal Inference: Generalized Latent Factor Models with Missingness and Implicit Regularization
